item.title: Musk v. Altman Kicks Off, DOJ Guts Voting Rights Unit, and Is the AI Job Apocalypse Overhyped?
item.description: In this episode of Uncanny Valley, we get into how the Elon Musk-Sam Altman trial goes way beyond their rivalry and could have major implications both for OpenAI and also the AI industry at large.

item.title: Elon Musk Seemingly Admits xAI Has Used OpenAI’s Models to Train Its Own
item.description: While answering questions under oath, Musk argued it’s standard practice for AI labs to use their competitors’ models.

item.title: OpenAI Rolls Out ‘Advanced’ Security Mode for At-Risk Accounts
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out Advanced Account Security for people concerned that their ChatGPT or Codex accounts could be potential targets of phishing attacks.

item.title: These Men Allegedly Profit Off Teaching People How to Make AI Porn
item.description: Three Arizona women have filed a lawsuit against a group of men that alleges they used the women’s photos to make AI porn influencers, then offered online courses showing others how to do it.

item.title: Reid Hoffman Thinks Doctors Should Ask AI for a Second Opinion
item.description: The LinkedIn cofounder now has an AI drug discovery startup—and thinks not asking chatbots for medical advice is “bordering on committing malpractice.”

item.title: How Elon Musk Squeezed OpenAI: They ‘Are Gonna Want to Kill Me’
item.description: Tensions flared on the third day of trial in Musk v. Altman as OpenAI’s lawyers cross-examined Musk.

item.title: Emergency First Responders Say Waymos Are Getting Worse
item.description: “I believe the technology was deployed too quickly in too vast amounts, with hundreds of vehicles, when it wasn’t really ready,” one police official told federal regulators last month.

item.title: Taylor Swift Wants to Trademark Her Likeness. These TikTok Deepfake Ads Show Why
item.description: Researchers show scammers are using AI-manipulated footage of celebrity interviews to trick users into sharing their personal data.

item.title: Sanctioned Chinese AI Firm SenseTime Releases Image Model Built for Speed
item.description: With US restrictions limiting its access to advanced tech, SenseTime is doubling down on open source with a new model optimized to run on Chinese-made chips.

item.title: I've Covered Robots for Years. This One Is Different
item.description: From sorting chicken nuggets to screwing in lightbulbs, Eka’s robotic claw feels like we're approaching a ChatGPT moment for the physical world.
